front: Which criteria are used to mark a teaching presentation (microteaching)?
back: Content; demonstration; clarity of presentation and explanation; interaction with learners; time management and pacing; questioning; and closure.
refs: WEB Indian J Pharmacol Microteaching: overview and examination evaluation 2023 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10657622/

front: How often must teaching skills be assessed during MD Pharmacology training (NMC)?
back: At least two sessions dedicated to assessing teaching skills every year; good teaching practice is assessed in every academic activity the PG conducts. The log book, signed by the head of department, is produced in original at the final practical exam.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (teaching-learning methods I and J: teaching skills, log book)

front: What presentation skills must an MD Pharmacology PG demonstrate (NMC)?
back: Presentation skills in a classroom setting and at academic meetings at local and national levels.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (psychomotor competencies, mandatory 6)

front: Describe Pendleton's rules for giving feedback.
back: The learner first says what went well; the observer then says what went well; the learner says what could be improved; the observer then says what could be improved. The method is learner-led and encourages self-reflection.
refs: WEB BMC Med Educ Feedback in the clinical setting 2020 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7712594/

front: What is the "sandwich" method of feedback, and its drawback?
back: A point to improve sits between two positive comments. It is weakened because learners expect the criticism and discount the constructive content.
refs: WEB Cureus Development and evaluation of the Joseph-RATA structured feedback model in undergraduate pharmacology 2026 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13589777/

front: Case: a PG gave a rushed lecture with crowded slides. How should the faculty give feedback, and why?
back: Plan the time and a private, confidential place, and talk about observed behaviour (timing, slide density), not personality. A structured model such as Pendleton's lets the PG self-assess first, so the PG owns the problems, then the observer adds specific points and both agree an action plan, for example fewer words per slide and a rehearsed time plan. Re-observe later to close the loop.
refs: WEB BMC Med Educ Feedback in the clinical setting 2020 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7712594/

front: Which unit trains MD Pharmacology PG students in education methods and assessment techniques (NMC)?
back: The Medical Education Unit (MEU) or Department of Medical Education (DOME).
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (teaching-learning methods I)

front: Which two curricula must an MD Pharmacology PG be aware of for teaching (NMC)?
back: The salient features of the undergraduate medical curriculum in India, and the postgraduate medical education curriculum and guidelines in India.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (competency A, Teaching and Assessment 1 and 2)

front: What teaching skill does PGMER 2023 list among PG training goals?
back: Basic skills in teaching medical and paramedical professionals; PGs should become competent specialists and medical teachers.

front: Why does the NMC pair faculty observation of a PG's UG class with feedback?
back: Observation alone only records performance. Feedback turns it into learning, so the PG can correct weak teaching skills before the next session. This is the micro-teaching cycle: plan, teach, observe, feedback, re-plan, re-teach.
refs: NMC MD Pharmacology 2022 curriculum (training in teaching skills, I)
WEB Indian J Pharmacol Microteaching: overview and examination evaluation 2023 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10657622/

front: Why must a PG know the UG curriculum before planning a class?
back: The lesson objectives, depth and level of detail must fit what the undergraduates are expected to learn and already know. Without this, objectives are pitched too high or too low.
